reports.title: ` NYSE: TBN, ASX: TBN 1Q FY27 Result Presentation Mr. Todd Abbott – Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer November 12, 2026

desk.headline: First Beetaloo gas sales: 0.31 Bcf and $1.8m revenue; no financial guidance, take-or-pay contract due early 2027
results: Tamboran and partner Daly Waters Energy became the first to sell gas from the Beetaloo Basin, starting in early September; Tamboran's share was 0.31 Bcf worth $1.8m.
Gas revenue and direct costs were capitalised because the plant is still being commissioned, so they are not yet in EBITDAX, which was -$14.5m.
Well tests backed earlier results: SS2-3H and SS2-5H averaged 8.8 and 10.0 MMcf/d over 30 days, and the re-opened SS2-2H ST1 averaged 10.2 MMcf/d.
The gas compression plant was finished on time and is expected to come in about $10m under budget; three more wells were drilled on the SS1 pad.
Capex rose to $56.9m and cash fell to $165m (net cash $128m); first cash from gas sales arrived in early November.

guidance.summary: No revenue or earnings guidance. The company expects to finish commissioning the plant in Q4 2026 and to start the fixed-price take-or-pay contract with the Northern Territory Government in Q1 2027, when it is paid for 40 TJ/day regardless of demand.

watch: Start of the take-or-pay contract in Q1 2027 and when gas revenue begins to show in earnings.
Fracking of the three SS1 wells (Q4 2026 / Q1 2027) and the Santos-operated EP 161 appraisal wells.
Cash burn and progress on the strategic partnership needed for more Orion drilling.
